execution_kind: CPU only on existing archived data, no simulator/evaluator
observation: Head-only updates had26% greater old-late-state KL at matched currentKL in3/3 archived assisted-policy batches. Feature freezing alone is not a locality mechanism.
hypothesis: A trust metric including prior states admits useful current-distribution readout movement while protecting old-state action mapping.
competing: Old/current action sensitivities overlap too strongly: protecting old states consumes the apparent current policy-gradient signal.
gate: In>=2/3 batches oldKL(candidate)/oldKL(current-only)<=.5 and linear surrogate gain ratio>=.8 and finite clipped surrogate gain>0; exact executed KL within1% of analytic current/old KL
formula: U=G(C_current+lambda*C_old+ridge*I)^-1, scaled to fixed current Gaussian mean-KL .01; output-layer update compiled into unchanged MLP
scope: Fixed hidden features/critic/std; analytic tangent policy-gradient trade-off, not a complete PPO training procedure or task performance
prior_reference: Same first64 original BC training episodes, t30:50. Candidate metric consumes these old states; both methods share historical assets/costs. No teacher action labels used by metric.
followup: Only a passed geometry gate permits registering a fresh public paired forward/reverse diagnostic. No full training or protected holdout.
novelty: Old-state KL/Fisher retention and constrained readout learning are established ideas; no novelty claim
